title: Standard-model perfection of a closed immersion pushforward
statement: Let i:Z→Y be a closed immersion of schemes, with a specified derived localization of O_Y-modules and localizations of the same Hom universe on every open of Y [def-pc-derived-category]. Assume the single i_*O_Z[0] is perfect on Y [def-pc-perfect-complex]. Then the standard derived direct image [def-pc-derived-direct-image] of the standard tensor unit on Z [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure] is perfect in the standard derived model of Y (using standard localizations on its opens). No properness, Noetherianity, right adjoint, or object K is assumed.

source.place: Tags 0A9U, 08CM and 05RU, comparison step before the second equality of Tag 0BRT

proof.text: For each original local witness on U, commute exact restriction with the single functor using Functor.mapDerivedCategorySingleFunctor. Use DerivedCategory.singleFunctorIsoCompQ to turn its isomorphism into Q(single(M|U)) ≅ Q(K). Apply Localization.uniq to the old and standard Q localizations, and compose its compUniqFunctor components, to obtain the corresponding isomorphism in the standard localization. Commute standard restriction with single again. This keeps the same U, point membership, K and IsStrictlyPerfect proof, and proves standardSinglePerfect without any global restriction-comparison lemma.

Apply the already proved closedImmersion_pushforward_preservesCokernel to every module morphism. The scheme and ringed-space pushforward functors agree definitionally. Additivity and Functor.preservesFiniteColimits_of_preservesCokernels give finite-colimit preservation; the sheaf pushforward right-adjoint instance gives finite-limit preservation. Thus Functor.singleFunctorCompRightDerivedFunctorIso identifies the derived pushforward of any single module with the single ordinary pushforward.

In the standard derived tensor structure, the tensor unit is definitionally the degree-zero single of the structure module (Iso.refl). Map this isomorphism through derived pushforward and compose with the exact-functor single comparison. For each local witness from step 1, map the resulting global isomorphism through standard restriction and compose with that witness. This proves exactly the given IsPerfect conclusion, including empty schemes and empty opens.

lean.statement:
theorem perfectImmersion_standardPerfection
    {Z Y : Scheme.{u}} (i : Z ⟶ Y) [IsClosedImmersion i]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{wY} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : Y.Opens, HasDerivedCategory.{wY}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (hperfect : Y.IsPerfect
      ((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor
        (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace)) 0).obj
        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward i).obj (SheafOfModules.unit Z.ringCatSheaf)))) :
    @Scheme.IsPerfect Y (HasDerivedCategory.standard _)
      (fun _ ↦ HasDerivedCategory.standard _)
      ((@schemeDerivedDirectImage Z Y (HasDerivedCategory.standard _)
        (HasDerivedCategory.standard _) i).obj
        (𝟙_ (@schemeDerivedCategory Z (HasDerivedCategory.standard _))))
